• $c = b+2$
• $a+b+c=10$
Prove, by exhaustion, that the product of $a$, $b$ and $c$ is always even.
You may use the table below to illustrate your answer.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Any one correct row for $b=1$, $b=2$ or $b=3$ (e.g. $a=6,b=1,c=3$; $a=4,b=2,c=4$; $a=2,b=3,c=5$). Products do not need to be found for this mark.
M1: Attempts the product $abc$ for at least 2 valid combinations.
A1*: Requires all three valid combinations with correct products (18, 32, 30), no other combinations shown unless crossed out or discounted, and a (minimal) conclusion e.g. the product of $a$, $b$ and $c$ is even, hence proven, QED.
Algebraic/logic approach: B1: Uses the information to obtain a correct equation connecting $a$ and $b$ e.g. $a+2b=8$, $a=8-2b$. M1: States $a$ must be even and considers the product $abc$ in some way. A1*: States e.g. $abc$ is even with a reason e.g. "even $\times$ anything is even".

questions.stem:
A curve $C$ has equation $y=\mathrm{f}(x)$ where
$\mathrm{f}(x)=(2-kx)^5$
and $k$ is a constant.
Given that when $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is divided by $(4x-5)$ the remainder is $\frac{243}{32}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that $k=\frac{2}{5}$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Substitutes $x=\frac{5}{4}$ into $\mathrm{f}(x)$, equates to $\frac{243}{32}$ and attempts to make $k$ the subject by taking the $5^{\mathrm{th}}$ root of both sides.
A1*: $k=\frac{2}{5}$ with no errors and sufficient working shown. Accept as a minimum $(2-k\times\frac{5}{4})=\frac{3}{2}\Rightarrow k=\frac{2}{5}$. Note that just $(2-k\times\frac{5}{4})^5=\frac{243}{32}\Rightarrow k=\frac{2}{5}$ scores no marks as the minimum for the M mark requires taking the 5th root of both sides.
Alternative by verification: M1: Substitutes $k=\frac{2}{5}$ and $x=\frac{5}{4}$ and attempts to raise an evaluated $2-kx$ to the power of 5. A1: Fully correct work and makes a (minimal) conclusion e.g. Hence proven, QED, Therefore true, etc.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Note that just $(2-\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{5}{4})^5=\frac{243}{32}$ or $(2-\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{5}{4})^5=(2-\frac{1}{2})^5=\frac{243}{32}$ scores no marks as the $2-\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{5}{4}$ or $2-\frac{1}{2}$ must be evaluated for the M mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the first three terms, in ascending powers of $x$, of the binomial expansion of $\left(2-\frac{2}{5}x\right)^5$
giving each term in simplest form.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts the binomial expansion to obtain the correct structure for the $x$ or $x^2$ term i.e. the correct binomial coefficient with the correct power of 2 and the correct power of $\pm\frac{2}{5}x$. The binomial coefficients do not have to be evaluated but must be correct if they are.
A1: For the correct simplified $x$ or $x^2$ term i.e. $-32x$ or $+\frac{64}{5}x^2$.
A1: For $32-32x+\frac{64}{5}x^2$ which may be written as a list. Allow equivalents for $\frac{64}{5}$ e.g. $12.8$. Condone $32+(-32x)+\frac{64}{5}x^2$. Ignore any extra terms but do not isw – mark their final answer. If they don't simplify in (b) do not allow simplified terms in (c) as recovery.
Alternative takes out a power of 2: score M1 for $2^5(...\pm5\times\pm\frac{1}{5}x+...)$ or $2^5(...\frac{5\times4}{2}(\pm\frac{1}{5}x)^2+...)$, then A marks as above.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- If awarding this mark for the $x^2$ term you can condone missing brackets e.g. $\pm{}^5C_2\times2^3\times\pm\frac{2}{5}x^2$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Using the solution to part (b) and making your method clear,
(c) find the gradient of $C$ at the point where $x=0$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts to differentiate their expansion and substitutes $x=0$ which may be implied. For the differentiation, look for $x^n \to x^{n-1}$ at least once including $k\to0$ or $kx\to k$.
A1ft: $-32$ following correct differentiation, or follow through on their $q$ provided the expansion in (b) was of the form $p+qx+rx^2$, $p,q,r\neq0$, and the differentiation is correct for their $p+qx+rx^2$ i.e. $q+2rx$. In part (c) you can also ignore any extra terms e.g. do not penalise if they have differentiated any of the extra terms incorrectly in an otherwise correct solution.

questions.stem:
The weight of a baby mammal is monitored over a 16-month period.
The weight of the mammal, $w$ kg, is given by
$w = \log_a(t+5) - \log_a 4 \qquad 2 \leqslant t \leqslant 18$
where $t$ is the age of the mammal in months and $a$ is a constant.
Given that the weight of the mammal was $10$ kg when $t=3$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that $a = 1.072$ correct to 3 decimal places.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Substitutes $t=3$ and $w=10$ into the equation and achieves $\log_a 2 = 10$ or e.g. $\log_a\frac{8}{4}=10$ correctly.
M1: Correctly removes the log to obtain $a^{10}="2"$.
A1*: Fully correct proof showing $a=2^{1/10}$ or $a=\sqrt[10]{2}$ or $a=\sqrt[10]{\frac{8}{4}}$ and obtains awrt $1.072$. Note that this may be implied by the accuracy of their $a$ e.g. $1.071773463\ldots$ so allow for $1.0718$ (rounded) or $1.0717$ (truncated). May also see logarithm approach e.g. $a^{10}=2\Rightarrow \log a^{10}=\log2\Rightarrow \log a=\frac{\log2}{10}\Rightarrow a=10^{\log2/10}=\ldots$ or using $\ln$. False solutions: $10=\log_a8-\log_a4\Rightarrow\frac{\log_a8}{\log_a4}=10\Rightarrow\log_a2=10\Rightarrow a^{10}=2\Rightarrow a=\sqrt[10]{2}=1.072$ scores M0M1A0; $10=\log_a8-\log_a4\Rightarrow\frac{8\log a}{4\log a}=10\Rightarrow2\log a=10\Rightarrow\log a^2=10\Rightarrow a^{10}=2\Rightarrow a=\sqrt[10]{2}=1.072$ scores no marks.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Using $a = 1.072$
(b) find an equation for $t$ in terms of $w$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Applies the subtraction law for logs to write the equation as $w = \log_{1.072}\left(\frac{t+5}{4}\right)$.
M1: Writes the equation as $1.072^w = f(t)$ and proceeds to make $t$ the subject.
A1: $t = 4\times1.072^w - 5$.
Alternative: M1: Rearranges to make $\log_{1.072}(t+5)$ the subject correctly, i.e. $w+\log_{1.072}4 = \log_{1.072}(t+5)$. M1: Removes the logs on lhs to obtain $t+5=1.072^{w+\log_{1.072}4}$. A1: $t=1.072^{w+\log_{1.072}4}-5$. In both cases allow the use of "$a$" or a more accurate value for "$a$" rather than $1.072$ for both method marks.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) find the value of $t$ when $w=15$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Substitutes $w=15$ into their equation from (b) or possibly the given equation $w=\log_{1.072}(t+5)-\log_{1.072}4$ and proceeds to find a value for $t$.
A1: awrt $6.35$ (months) (NB If full accuracy used for $a$ answer is $6.3137\ldots$ and scores A0). Ignore any units if given.

See possible rearrangements e.g. $3^x\times2^{x+4}=6\Rightarrow\log_2 3^x+\log_2 2^{x+4}=\log_2 6$, or $3^x\times2^x\times2^4=6\Rightarrow\log_2 3^x+\log_2 2^x+\log_2 2^4=\log_2 6$, or $3^x\times2^{x+3}=3\Rightarrow\log_2 3^x+\log_2 2^{x+3}=\log_2 3$, or $3^x\times2^x=\frac{3}{8}\Rightarrow\log_2 3^x+\log_2 2^x=\log_2\frac{3}{8}$, or $3^{x-1}\times2^{x+3}=1\Rightarrow\log_2 3^{x-1}+\log_2 2^{x+3}=\log_2 1$.
B1: The correct power law seen for logs. Allow this mark to score independently so sight of e.g. $\log_2 2^x=x\log_2 2$, $\log_2 3^x=x\log_2 3$, $\log_2 6^x=x\log_2 6$, $\log_2 2^{x+4}=(x+4)\log_2 2$ etc can score this mark. (Condone e.g. $\log_2 2^{x+4}=x+4\log_2 2$ for this mark.)
dM1: Correct method to make $x$ the subject. Condone slips in rearrangement but there must be more than one term in $x$. Award for collecting terms in $x$ on one side and non $x$ terms on the other side, factorising and then dividing. Dependent on the first method mark.
A1: $\frac{a-3}{a+1}$ or e.g. $\frac{3-a}{-a-1}$. Note that candidates are unlikely to be working in anything other than base 2 so you can condone the omission of the base throughout. For reference, $\frac{a-3}{a+1}=-0.54741122\ldots$ which may be useful in some circumstances.
Alternative not requiring the addition law (using base 6): M1: Divides by $2^4$, takes logs of both sides and writes $3^x\times2^x$ as $6^x$. B1: $\log_2 6^x=x\log_2 6$ (may be implied). dM1: Makes $x$ the subject. A1: $\frac{a-3}{a+1}$ or e.g. $\frac{3-a}{-a-1}$.
Alternative not requiring logs: B1: $a=\log_2 3\Rightarrow 3=2^a$. M1: Attempts to write all terms as powers of 2. dM1: Combines and equates powers and makes $x$ the subject as in main scheme. A1: $\frac{a-3}{a+1}$ or e.g. $\frac{3-a}{-a-1}$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Note that this may follow incorrect work e.g. $3^x\times2^{x+4}=6\Rightarrow\log_2 3^x\times\log_2 2^{x+4}=\log_2 6\Rightarrow x\log_2 3\times(x+4)\log_2 2^{x+4}=\log_2 6$
- dM1 examples: $x\log_2 3+(x+4)\log_2 2=\log_2 6\Rightarrow x(\log_2 3+\log_2 2)=\log_2 6-4\Rightarrow x=...$ or $(x-1)\log_2 3+(x+3)\log_2 2=0\Rightarrow ax+x=a-3\Rightarrow x=...$
- Alternative using change of base: $3^x\times2^{x+4}=6\Rightarrow2^{x+3}=3^{1-x}\Rightarrow\log2^{x+3}=\log3^{1-x}\Rightarrow(x+3)\log2=(1-x)\log3\Rightarrow(x+3)\frac{\log_2 2}{\log_2 10}=(1-x)\frac{\log_2 3}{\log_2 10}\Rightarrow x+3=a(1-x)\Rightarrow x(a+1)=a-3\Rightarrow x=...$ Score as: M1: Divides by 2 and $3^x$ and takes logs of both sides B1: E.g. $\log2^{x+3}=(x+3)\log2$ or $\log3^{1-x}=(1-x)\log3$ dM1: Changes to base 2 correctly and makes x the subject as main scheme A1: $\frac{a-3}{a+1}$ or e.g. $\frac{3-a}{-a-1}$
- Alternative using logs base 6: $3^x\times2^{x+4}=6\Rightarrow3^x\times2^x=\frac{3}{8}\Rightarrow6^x=\frac{3}{8}\Rightarrow\log_6 6^x=\log_6\frac{3}{8}\Rightarrow x\log_6 6=\log_6\frac{3}{8}$, $x=\log_6\frac{3}{8}=\frac{\log_2\frac{3}{8}}{\log_2 6}=\frac{\log_2 3-\log_2 8}{\log_2 3+\log_2 2}=\frac{a-3}{a+1}$ M1: Divides by $2^4$, writes $3^x\times2^x$ as $6^x$ and takes logs base 6 of both sides which may be implied by e.g. $6^x=\frac{3}{8}\Rightarrow x=\log_6\frac{3}{8}$ B1: For $\log_6 6^x=x\log_6 6$ (may be implied) dM1: Changes to log base 2 correctly (and makes x the subject) A1: Correct expression

questions.question_text:
Given $a=\log_2 3$
(i) write, in simplest form, in terms of $a$,
(a) $\log_2 9$
(b) $\log_2\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{16}\right)$
(3)
(ii) Solve
$3^x \times 2^{x+4} = 6$
giving your answer, in simplest form, in terms of $a$.
(4)
